subject: Private Site Commissioning: final sanity sweep, rollforward criteria, and readout
messages:
From: Sasha Kravitz <sasha.kravitz@acmecloud.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private site commissioning: final sanity sweep and go/no-go criteria

Markus / team,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We took the internal checklist and ran a light verification on the fabric side this morning. Before we schedule the final cutover window we need:

- a concise runbook extract of the smoke tests you plan to run during the first 60 minutes (we'll use it in our change advisory)
- clear rollforward/rollback criteria and expected time-to-recover per step
- an evidence bundle (logs + short playback) for KV cache priming and TLS cert rotation

I've attached our local commissioning-checklist with comments. Proposed cutover window: Thu Nov 19, 00:00-02:00 UTC (our night). We can shift if you need more time.

Can you confirm you can provide the runbook extract and the KV priming evidence by EOD PT today? Sasha will be on the bridge for the window.

Attachments: commissioning-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Sasha Kravitz
Cloud Ops Lead, Acme Cloud
ops@acmecloud.com

---

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Kravitz <sasha.kravitz@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private site commissioning: final sanity sweep and go/no-go criteria

Sasha,

Thanks — we can deliver what you asked. High level plan (deliverables by EOD PT):

1) Runbook extract (attached) — sequence of smoke tests for first 60 minutes, owner, and expected results.
2) Rollforward/rollback matrix — threshold-based decisions (latency, error-rate, kv-miss-rate) and expected recovery steps.
3) KV priming evidence — we will capture the first 10 minutes of K/V warmup metrics and attach logs.
4) Cert rotation checklist and verification commands.

I've attached a trimmed runbook (redwood-runbook-v1.md) with the smoke steps you'll need to paste into your CAB notes. Key callouts:
- Step 3 (KV priming) is a warmup phase that we run for 8 minutes; if warmup rate < 60% throughput after 12 minutes we trigger the rollback sequence described in the matrix.
- Telemetry probes: token-level latency, 95p tail, kv-cache-hit-rate, and open socket counts.

I'll ask Irene to start a short warmup run now against the staging fabric and post the logs here. If anything looks off we'll propose a 2-hour later window to avoid your midnight ops.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-runbook-v1.md (markdown)

---

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Kravitz <sasha.kravitz@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private site commissioning: final sanity sweep and go/no-go criteria

Markus / team — quick update from the warmup we kicked off at 11:15 PT:

- KV priming completed but observed a slow ramp between minute 4-9 on the priming job; the hit-rate reached 85% by minute 9 (target is 90% by minute 8).
- We captured a short log snippet and the warmup metrics; attaching kv-warmup.log.
- Root cause candidate: concurrent background GC on the node hosting the priming process + slightly undersized kube pod CPU request. We saw CPU throttling spikes around 11:18:23.

Recommendations:
- Option A (preferred): shift the cutover +30 minutes and increase the priming job CPU request by 30% for the warmup window; rerun warmup to confirm stable 90% hit rate by minute 8.
- Option B: keep the window but extend the warmup phase from 8 -> 12 minutes and accept an extra 4 minutes of risk with explicit rollback thresholds (we'll tighten observability and be ready to roll back at minute 12).

If we pick A I'll make the change and post a rerun summary within 25 minutes. If we pick B we need to update the runbook and CAB notes to match changed timing. Either way we should capture the priming evidence bundle for your audit.

Logs attached: kv-warmup.log (text, 42KB)

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

---

From: Sasha Kravitz <sasha.kravitz@acmecloud.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private site commissioning: final sanity sweep and go/no-go criteria

Team — thanks for the quick triage. We prefer Option A: shift the window by +30m and rerun. That keeps our rollback exposure lower.

Action items as I see them:
- Redwood: bump priming CPU requests, rerun warmup, post final kv-warmup.log and the short warmup metrics snapshot in the evidence bundle (by 16:00 PT).
- Acme: will update CAB notes and confirm bridge participation; we will still hold the target date but start at 00:30 UTC if all looks good.
- Both: once the evidence bundle is posted, we will run a 30-minute pre-cutover checklist on the bridge and then proceed.

Markus — can you confirm you'll post the rerun artifacts by 16:00 PT? If so we'll circulate the updated change and finalize the DocuSign sign-off link.

Regards,
Sasha
Cloud Ops Lead, Acme Cloud
